what_i_did: Per the art director, the hero is the only target (there is no turnaround). make_views.py keys the hero against a per-row backdrop estimate (the cream darkens down the frame), keeps the warm-white daisy petals with a brighter-and-bluer test, and drops the cast shadow left of the first stone. The result is views/hero_mask.png.

hero_check.py renders from the hero's direction: 16 deg off the front towards -X (the near end of the row is on the left), 8 deg up, at 1.0 x the bbox diagonal with the lens shortened in proportion (harness framing, stronger perspective). Calibrated over yaw/elevation/distance grids (flat at 0.78 to 0.82 around the pick), then held fixed.

The old GF-010 is 1.25 m long along X, 0.43 m deep and 0.22 m tall, and to_game copies the GLB as-is, so the row keeps the 1.25 m length along X. Eight stones at the brief's 0.30 x 0.25 x 0.22 m would make a 2.4 m row, so the stones keep those proportions scaled to 0.166 x 0.138 x 0.128 m (with +-7% size and +-12 deg yaw variation), touching at a 0.155 m pitch.

Each stone is a faceted squashed boulder: four staggered rings of 9 jittered vertices (widest a third of the way up, rounded shoulders) and a top point, with an open bottom on the ground, 63 triangles each. Six are Stone_Grey, two (3rd and 7th) Stone_Pale.

Eight daisies (Petal_White star discs of 11 broad petals for the big ones, 7 for the small, with a domed Flower_Yellow centre) and seven marigolds (cupped 10-point Petal_Yellow stars), on 2-triangle Leaf_Green stem ribbons. Heads turn toward the hero camera. The big daisies sit low against the stone faces in the gaps, as in the hero; the small ones and the marigolds poke just above the stones from behind.

973 triangles (flower/ground plant budget 1k) in 6 meshes, one flat material each: Stone_Grey, Stone_Pale, Petal_White, Petal_Yellow, Flower_Yellow, Leaf_Green. Origin at the centre of the row on the ground, row along X, front -Y. No animation, no variants (plant). to_game.py stone-edging installs simulations/regional-assets/GF-010.glb.
good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.808 at the final 768 px / 48 samples (0.822 at 384 px): the low row of eight rounded stones with flowers poking above and big daisies in the front gaps matches the hero's outline.
Chunky colour blocks: grey stones, white daisy stars with yellow eyes, yellow marigolds, green tufts all read at small size.
Same length (1.25 m) and orientation (along X) as the old GF-010, under the 1k budget at 973 triangles.
off: Stones are 0.17 m long, not the brief's 0.30 m: eight 0.30 m stones cannot fit in the old 1.25 m row that the game uses unscaled. Proportions are kept. The row is 0.18 m tall (old 0.22 m) and 0.27 m deep (old 0.43 m, which was off-centre in depth).
The hero's stones carry many small facets; mine have 9 x 4 facets each to stay at 1k. The silhouette is right but they read a little smoother and boxier than the hero's.
The hero's dense leafy clumps at the base are thinner here (16 four-leaf tufts in the gaps), and the tiny base daisies in the hero are left out; both would be a few pixels in the tile.
Flower stems are flat ribbons turned to the hero camera, so they thin out when seen edge-on from other angles.

rounds.change: First build: 8 jittered 7x4 dome boulders, 10 daisies and 7 marigolds on tall stems, 22 base tufts; camera -26/8 at dist 1.3 cropped the near end.
Rounder, rounded-box boulder profile (8 segments), flowers lowered with bigger heads, stems as 2-triangle ribbons; camera fixed at -16/8 with a shortened lens so the whole row stays in frame.
Bigger front daisies (r 0.044) low on the stone faces, tufts moved into the gaps, warmer stone and darker leaf colours; end tufts stuck out past the row (0.766).
Tufts only in the gaps, stone pitch fitted so the stones span exactly 1.25 m.
9-segment stones with rounder shoulders, bigger tuft leaves. Final render at 768 px / 48 samples scores 0.808.

moving_parts: None: a static plant prop (the game poses and sways plants itself).
creative_additions: Flower heads turned toward the viewer, cupped marigold heads for volume, and staggered facet rings so each stone looks chipped rather than turned.
